response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.throws AS throws, COUNT(DISTINCT ma.player_id) AS cnt FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON p.player_id = ma.player_id GROUP BY p.throws), s AS (SELECT throws, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS share FROM g), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s), k AS (SELECT s.*, a.avg_share FROM s, a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM k

assumptions.assumption: The average share across hands is the simple mean of the per-group shares (including the NULL group), computed over all groups before filtering. Since shares sum to 1, this equals 1/number of groups.
Missing throws values (NULL, from matched players) form their own group; empty-string values, if any, would be a separate group and are not treated as NULL.
The average share returned is the mean share among the kept hands, and the excess is each kept hand's share minus the overall average share across all hands.
